title: Time-varying effects of revascularisation versus medical therapy on spontaneous MI and cardiac death in stable coronary disease: reconstructed-IPD network meta-analysis

pico.population: Adults with chronic coronary syndrome, stratified by presentation, ischaemia burden, anatomy and LV function
pico.intervention: Routine revascularisation (PCI or CABG) plus medical therapy, including FFR-guided PCI
pico.comparator: Initial medical therapy alone, or sham/placebo PCI where available
pico.outcomes: Cardiac death, spontaneous MI, all-cause death, with time-varying hazard ratios and restricted mean survival time
pico.timing: Follow-up from randomisation to the longest reported, 1 to 15 years

decision: Whether and when to offer revascularisation for prognosis, not only symptoms, in stable coronary disease, and how to counsel on early procedural hazard against later spontaneous-MI benefit.
decision_maker: Interventional cardiologists, heart teams and guideline committees
why_now: Two meta-analyses reached different conclusions on cardiac death (PMIDs 32794407, 34002203), and trials since, including extended ISCHEMIA follow-up (36335918), long-term FAME follow-up (41540107), REVIVED (36027563) and the ISCHEMIA CTO analysis (40139890), report non-proportional effects that trial-level relative risks cannot capture.

competing.note: ISCHEMIA-CTO: CTO subpopulation only, MACE at 5 years
PCI-GULF: ischaemic cardiomyopathy with reduced LVEF only

designs.primary: Reconstructed individual patient data network meta-analysis from published Kaplan-Meier curves, with flexible parametric or RMST models and prespecified effect modification by ischaemia, anatomy and LV function
designs.alternative: One-stage IPD meta-analysis if ISCHEMIA, FAME 2 and REVIVED investigators share data

data_required: Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk for cardiac death, spontaneous MI and all-cause death from the randomised revascularisation versus medical therapy trials, with MI definitions per trial
data_sources: Trial investigators for IPD where available
feasibility: High for the reconstructed-IPD analysis, which is the owner's established method; MI definition heterogeneity across eras is the main technical risk. IPD route would need a consortium.
overlap: No overlap with the active non-culprit lesion NMA in STEMI (different population and comparison).
target_journal: Circulation or JACC (European Heart Journal as alternative)

G1.note: PCI for stable coronary disease is among the most common procedures; the decision concerns death and MI.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. The two pooled analyses disagree on cardiac death (RR 0.79, 0.67-0.93 versus all-cause RR 0.99, 0.90-1.09 in different outcome sets, PMIDs 34002203 and 32794407).

G3.note: No adequately powered RCT of the whole comparison reports within 24 months; ongoing trials cover CTO (NCT03563417, 2028-11) or ischaemic cardiomyopathy (NCT07349979, 2028-01; NCT05828719, 2028-07). Latest meta-analyses in the subset are from 2020 and 2021; trials published since include REVIVED (700 patients, PMID 36027563). A search outside the appraised subset for a 2024 to 2026 target-journal meta-analysis is still required.

G4.note: Reconstructed-IPD time-varying analysis addresses non-proportional hazards, which fixed relative risks cannot; a guideline committee would cite it. A conventional meta-analysis would repeat the existing disagreement.

G5.note: Not a repeat of the same trials: adds post-2021 trials and a different estimand. Risk that the added sample is modest; the adversarial check should quantify the added patients.

impact.why: Stable coronary disease PCI and CABG decisions are very frequent and concern hard outcomes.

novelty.why: Meta-analyses exist, but time-varying effects by presentation have not been shown in the appraised subset.

equipoise.why: Pooled analyses and individual trials disagree on cardiac death and spontaneous MI.

design.why: Reconstructed IPD is credible for time-to-event outcomes but limited by MI definition heterogeneity and the lack of covariates.

timeliness.why: Recent long-term follow-ups (PMIDs 36335918, 41540107) change the evidence, but no single readout forces the timing.

citation.why: Comparable synthesis papers appear in Circulation and EHJ (PMIDs 32794407, 34002203); the benchmark has not yet been run.

feasibility.why: Matches the owner's reconstructed-IPD and network meta-analysis skills.

next_actions: Register on PROSPERO and define MI and cardiac death mapping across trials.
Extract Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk from PMIDs 32227755, 36335918, 41540107, 36027563 and the trials in PMIDs 32794407 and 34002203.
Run a search outside the appraised subset for target-journal meta-analyses from 2024 to 2026 before committing.

status_history.reason: Generated from the D1 landscape; all gates passed with caveats on G3 and G5.

title: Effect modification of intravascular imaging-guided PCI by region, lesion complexity, ACS presentation and imaging modality: IPD meta-analysis of randomised trials

pico.population: Patients undergoing DES implantation in randomised imaging-guidance trials
pico.outcomes: Target vessel failure, cardiac death, target-vessel MI, TVR, with treatment-effect heterogeneity

decision: Which patients and settings should receive routine intravascular imaging, and whether benefit seen in Asian trials applies elsewhere.
decision_maker: Interventional cardiologists, cath lab directors, commissioners and guideline committees
why_now: Early trials were positive (PMIDs 36876735, 39236729, 37634149, 38604212), but 2026 trials in complex high-risk PCI and left main were neutral (41911016, 41911017) and one meta-analysis reports a geographic interaction (42879937).

competing.note: IMPROVE: IVUS in complex lesions, TVF at 12 months
ULTIMATE IV: IVUS in calcified lesions

designs.primary: One-stage IPD meta-analysis with prespecified interactions (region, complexity, ACS, modality, operator imaging experience)
designs.alternative: Reconstructed-IPD analysis plus trial-level meta-regression if IPD cannot be obtained

data_required: Patient-level data from 25 or more imaging-guidance RCTs, or reconstructed curves with subgroup data
feasibility: Low to moderate: needs a multi-trial IPD consortium; the owner can lead the statistical plan and the reconstructed fallback.
target_journal: Circulation, JACC or European Heart Journal

G1.note: Imaging use is a common cath-lab decision with cardiac death and MI endpoints.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. Trials conflict between early positive and 2026 neutral results.

G3.note: A JACC meta-analysis of 28 RCTs (24,634 patients, PMID 42747372) appeared in September 2026, and IMPROVE (3,100 patients, 2026-09), ULTIMATE IV, IVI-DIABETES and IVUS-CKD are due to report within 24 months. Trials published since PMID 42747372 are not yet quantified.

G4.note: IPD is the only design that can separate region from complexity, which trial-level meta-regression cannot.

G5.note: Not a repeat of the trial-level pooled estimates, but the geographic interaction is already reported at trial level (PMID 42879937).

impact.why: Imaging is used in a minority of PCIs in registry data (PMIDs 37464975, 42909189), so the decision is common and unsettled.

novelty.why: At least five meta-analyses already exist.

equipoise.why: Benefit is established in some settings and uncertain in others.

design.why: IPD with prespecified interactions would be cited.

timeliness.why: Several trials report within 24 months and could be added.

citation.why: Imaging meta-analyses appear in Lancet, BMJ and Circulation; the benchmark has not yet been run.

next_actions: Quantify trials and patients added since PMID 42747372 to settle the G3 objection.
Draft the interaction plan and approach trial leads for IPD sharing.

status_history.reason: Fails G3; recorded so the objection and the readout calendar are visible.

title: Operator and hospital volume thresholds for complex PCI: natural-experiment analysis in a national registry

pico.population: Patients undergoing PCI for CTO, left main, bifurcation, calcified or other complex lesions, and high-risk PCI
pico.intervention: Treatment at higher-volume operators and hospitals, with exposure defined by volume of complex procedures
pico.comparator: Treatment at lower-volume operators and hospitals
pico.outcomes: 30-day and long-term death, MI, stroke, major bleeding, procedural complications
pico.timing: Procedure date to 1 year and longer

decision: Whether to set minimum volumes or centralise complex PCI, and where to refer complex cases.
decision_maker: Commissioners, national audit bodies and professional societies; cardiologists referring cases
why_now: Registries disagree: no association with 30-day mortality in 133,970 British procedures (PMID 29579219) against lower in-hospital death at higher volume in 723,644 US procedures (PMID 30586696), and quasi-experimental access studies are appearing (PMIDs 42862553, 40742582).

designs.primary: Target trial emulation with hospital fixed effects and an instrument such as distance or referral-pathway change, in a national PCI registry linked to mortality

data_required: National PCI registry with lesion complexity, operator and hospital identifiers and linked long-term outcomes
data_sources: UK national PCI audit (access through collaborators, not confirmed in the owner profile)
SWEDEHEART or Danish registries via planned visits
feasibility: Low to moderate: the owner has BCIS shock registry access through collaborators, but PCI audit access is unconfirmed.
overlap: Conceptually adjacent to the owner's SRMA of cardiogenic shock care organisation; population and procedure differ, so no duplication.

G1.note: Volume thresholds affect where complex PCI is done and are tied to mortality.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. The two large registries disagree (PMIDs 29579219, 30586696).

G3.note: No RCT is feasible and none is registered in the trials file; no meta-analysis in the subset covers the question.

G4.note: A randomised comparison is impractical; a quasi-experimental design with explicit identification is the credible alternative. Instrument validity must be shown.

G5.note: Not an unadjusted operator-volume series: it targets complex-lesion volume and uses causal identification.

impact.why: Affects service design for a very common procedure.

novelty.why: Volume studies exist, but complex-lesion volume with causal design is less covered.

design.why: Quasi-experimental identification is credible but depends on instrument quality.

timeliness.why: No specific trigger beyond service reconfiguration debate.

citation.why: Volume papers have appeared in Circulation and EHJ (PMIDs 30586696, 29579219).

next_actions: Confirm access route to national PCI audit data with collaborators.
Define complex-PCI volume and candidate instruments.
Write the target trial protocol, including time zero and estimand.

status_history.reason: Generated from the D1 landscape; all gates passed, feasibility low.

title: PCI versus CABG in patients aged 75 years or older with multivessel or left main disease: target trial emulation in national registries

pico.population: Patients aged 75 years or older with multivessel or unprotected left main disease suitable for either strategy
pico.outcomes: All-cause death, MI, stroke, repeat revascularisation, major bleeding; 5-year restricted mean survival
pico.timing: Time zero at heart-team decision or index angiogram; follow-up 5 years

decision: Whether to recommend PCI or CABG for older patients with complex disease.
decision_maker: Heart teams, patients and guideline committees
why_now: Evidence conflicts and is mostly observational or a small subgroup: excess mortality with PCI in patients aged 74 or older (PMID 27009629) against no difference at 10 years in 575 elderly SYNTAXES patients (PMID 34082905); registry analyses in left main and NSTEMI favour CABG (PMIDs 37288564, 39601339).

competing.note: CABG or PCI in high-risk patients, 5-year analysis, reports 2032-12

designs.primary: Target trial emulation using clone-censor-weight methods in a national registry linked to surgical and PCI audits
designs.alternative: Pooled IPD from randomised trials with age-by-treatment interaction

data_required: National PCI and cardiac surgery audits with anatomical complexity, frailty proxies, linked mortality and hospital admissions
data_sources: UK national PCI and cardiac surgery audits (collaborator access, not confirmed)
feasibility: Moderate: SWEDEHEART-type analyses exist (PMID 37288564); confounding by frailty and anatomy requires careful design.

G1.note: Common decision in an ageing population with death as the outcome.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. Observational and randomised-subgroup results disagree (PMIDs 27009629, 34082905).

G3.note: No trial restricted to older patients is registered in the file; larger trials report from 2032 (NCT05534698) and RECHARGE:W/M (600 patients each) in 2033.

G4.note: A new RCT is unlikely to be funded soon; emulation with explicit time zero and frailty adjustment would be cited if identification is credible.

G5.note: Incremental risk is real because registry PCI versus CABG analyses exist; the contribution is the age-restricted, contemporary-stent design with prespecified estimand.

impact.why: Large and growing population with multivessel disease.

novelty.why: Several registry comparisons exist; older-age-specific target trial emulation less so.

equipoise.why: Conflicting data and no definitive trial.

design.why: Emulation is credible but residual confounding by frailty is the main threat.

timeliness.why: New randomised evidence is not due for years.

citation.why: Registry PCI versus CABG papers appear in EHJ and Circulation (PMIDs 37288564, 27009629).

feasibility.why: Registry access plausible through collaborators and visits but unconfirmed.

next_actions: Confirm registry access and available frailty proxies.
Write the target trial protocol with clone-censor-weight analysis.
Check outside the subset for recent age-specific PCI versus CABG analyses.

status_history.reason: Generated from the D1 landscape; all gates passed with a G5 caveat.

title: Preventive PCI for non-flow-limiting vulnerable coronary plaque: prospectively registered synthesis timed to the 2027 readouts

pico.population: Patients with angiographically non-flow-limiting lesions with high-risk plaque features on imaging, including after MI
pico.intervention: Preventive PCI (stent or drug-coated balloon) plus optimal medical therapy
pico.outcomes: Target-vessel or lesion failure, cardiac death, spontaneous target-vessel MI, with separation of hard and soft components

decision: Whether to treat non-flow-limiting vulnerable plaques invasively.
why_now: One randomised trial reported primary outcome in 0.4% versus 3.4% at 2 years but with components driven by softer events (PMID 38604213), and INTERCLIMA, NCT06855537 and RESTORE are due to report between 2027-01 and 2027-12.

competing.note: INTERCLIMA: cardiac death or spontaneous target-vessel MI

designs.primary: PROSPERO-registered pairwise meta-analysis with prespecified update as each trial reports, separating hard from soft components, with reconstructed IPD for time-to-event outcomes
designs.alternative: Decision model with value-of-information analysis for further trials

data_required: Published results of PMID 38604213 and each registered trial, with component-level event counts
feasibility: High: same-day synthesis workflow already in place.
overlap: Fits the owner's same-day SRMA workflow; no overlap with the non-culprit lesion NMA in STEMI beyond VULNERABLE (NCT05599061), which is a different question.
target_journal: JAMA Cardiology, Circulation or European Heart Journal

G1.note: Treating plaques that have not caused ischaemia would widen PCI indications; the endpoint question is hard versus soft events.

G2.note: Guideline position unverified (extracts not yet retrieved); G2 judged on trial evidence only. One positive trial with softer components and a small earlier trial (PMID 33069847).

G3.note: INTERCLIMA (1,425 patients, 2027-01), NCT06855537 (2,190, 2027-09) and RESTORE (1,860, 2027-12) will report within 24 months and each is adequately sized for its own comparison.

G4.note: A pre-registered pooled analysis with component separation would be citable once several trials report.

G5.note: Only meaningful after at least three trials report; today it would pool few studies, so the question is conditional on readouts.

impact.why: Non-flow-limiting lesions are common; a positive result would add a large PCI population.

novelty.why: No pooled synthesis in the subset; trials are new.

equipoise.why: One trial positive on soft components, others pending.

design.why: Pairwise pooling is credible once several large trials report; heterogeneity in plaque definition is a risk.

timeliness.why: Three trials report within 14 months of this date.

citation.why: Preventive PCI papers have appeared in the Lancet (PMID 38604213); benchmark not yet run.

next_actions: Register the protocol on PROSPERO with the update rule and component separation.
Pre-build extraction for PMID 38604213 and each registered trial.
Add the readouts to outputs/calendar.md with the pooling plan.

status_history.reason: Fails G3 as written; kept as a readout-timed synthesis for the calendar, not for the top ten.
